title: We All Can Make A Difference
verse: So the twelve called the whole group of the disciples together and said, “It is not right for us to neglect the word of God to wait on tables. But carefully select from among you, brothers, seven men who are well-attested, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may put in charge of this necessary task. But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of the word.” The proposal pleased the entire group, so they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, with Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas, a Gentile convert to Judaism from Antioch.
observation: The early days of the church seem full of motion and activity. As the church was growing, they were working out how to properly care for one another. The model of the synagogues of the time meant they had the duty to help one another in times of need. This is a great thing, but it can be overwhelming when the need is overwhelming. Instead of trying to do it all, the disciples realized their limitations. They also realized what was most important for them to do. They recognized they were not the only ones gifted. Everyone had the capacity to make a difference. This reality is still true today. We all have the ability to make a difference. Just like the disciples, we need to figure out what we can do and do it with all our might. Then, make room for someone else so they can make a difference, too. Then, we work together for the good of others and the glory of God.
application: How can you make a difference today?
prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for empowering us all to make a difference in our world.
